title: The City paid a firm $7.8 million after its president’s federal bid-rigging charge

beats.text: In 2013, officers of two Bay Area firms bid on a federal laboratory renovation.

visual.sub: bids to renovate a federal laboratory building

beats.text: According to the U.S. Attorney, the bids were rigged to lose to an undercover agent.

visual.label: The bids were not real
visual.sub: set above the bid of an undercover agent

beats.text: After the charge, the City paid one of those firms 7,754,088 dollars.

visual.label: paid by the City to Empire Engineering & Construction Inc.
visual.sub: in the fiscal years after its president was charged

beats.text: This is a lead, not a finding. Neither firm was charged, and a charge is an accusation.

visual.line: This is a lead, not a finding: a pattern in public records. This film says what the records show, what they do not show, and what would settle it.

beats.text: On April 7, 2017,

visual.text: a grand jury charged the “President of Empire Engineering and Construction, Inc. in Oakland and San Francisco”

beats.text: a grand jury charged Empire's president with conspiracy to defraud the United States.

visual.text: a grand jury charged the “President of Empire Engineering and Construction, Inc. in Oakland and San Francisco”

beats.text: On February 20, 2019, a federal jury convicted him on all counts.

visual.label: Convicted on all counts
visual.sub: conspiring to defraud the United States

beats.text: In July 2020 he was sentenced to 45 days in custody and a 4,000 dollar fine.
And since November 6, 2017, the firm itself has been suspended from federal awards. No end date.

visual.title: Federal exclusion list
visual.sub: EMPIRE ENGINEERING & CONSTRUCTION, INC., San Francisco, CA

beats.text: The suspension record's street address is the firm's own, in the City's business registry.

visual.label: The same street address
visual.sub: as the firm's address in the City's business registry

beats.text: Nine years on, it is still marked proceedings pending. No final decision.
But a federal suspension does not reach contracts paid for with City money.

visual.label: City money
visual.sub: a federal suspension does not reach it

beats.text: After the charge, the firm joined eight new City contract teams,

visual.label: new City contract teams after the charge

beats.text: with 5,868,892 dollars agreed.

visual.label: new City contract teams after the charge

beats.text: Five began after the federal suspension: 4,587,792 dollars.
Two Public Works contracts began in 2018, the last before the verdict.
Recreation and Park awarded one in September 2018. Did anyone ask about the federal case?
The payments peaked in fiscal 2020, at 3,976,783 dollars.

visual.label: City payments to Empire after the charge

beats.text: And 4,384,378 dollars came in the fiscal years after the jury's verdict.

visual.label: paid in the fiscal years after the verdict

beats.text: It is on none of the twelve City debarment reports read here.

visual.label: City debarment reports
visual.sub: the firm is in none of the twelve read

beats.text: The Controller notes that, unlike the federal government, the City cannot suspend contractors.

visual.line: Unlike the federal government, the City and the state cannot suspend contractors.

beats.text: A second firm, Townsend Management, is more weakly tied. A vice president was convicted too.
